_doc: Salt Creek Valley master plan, Phase 1 (planning only; Sean's brief of 2026-11-07, issue #467, PR #621's valley inputs). INERT: nothing in the game reads this file until Sean approves the geometry. The maps, profiles and tables are generated from it by tools/valley/valley_plan.py (never drawn by hand), so moving a point here moves it everywhere. Read with docs/briefs/valley-plan.md (the reasons, the DECIDED/PROPOSED/OPEN calls, the migration) and docs/briefs/valley-tables.md (generated: the coordinate schedule, travel times, grades, checks).

status_words.DECIDED: Sean's; not reopened without asking him.
status_words.PROPOSED: this plan's recommendation; a working value, never canon until Sean says so.

units.y: elevation in metres above the new Main Street crossroads' ground (Y 0). PROPOSED absolute: about 2,070 m above sea level (Durango 1,988 m; the La Plata foothills west of it 2,050-2,300 m)

frame.origin: the new town's crossroads: Main Street x North-South Street, at ground level. The new valley is a separate scene behind a switch (Sean, 2026-11-07 on #467), so it may reuse the old town's numbers without colliding with it.
frame.main_street_axis: Main Street runs due west (heading 270) along z 0, so the setting sun (DayCycle sun_azimuth 0) shines straight down it (DECIDED).
frame.precision: the playable valley stays within about 2.5 km of the origin: 32-bit positions keep better than a millimetre there.

envelope._doc: 4.4 x 3.6 km, 15.8 km2 (the DECIDED 'about 4 x 4 km' area). The town sits west of the middle, near the base of the western foothills (DECIDED, valley.md); the east holds the canyon, the trestle, the overpass and the widow; the south the open homestead and ranch country. Selective boundaries, never a wall of cliffs all round.

boundaries.how: the La Plata front: the foothills steepen past x -2000 into timbered slopes and broken mesas (climbable a little way, then too steep for a horse); the rail goes into its tunnel there.
past z -1400 the arroyo's headwater ridges and broken mesa country; the timber thins out; scenery beyond.

Salt Creek leaves through a narrowing gorge at the north-east (too rough to follow far); the rail leaves in a rock cut; the east road runs on toward Durango as a track whose far end is distance and the land's fold, not a wall.
rimrock mesas and broken canyon country (the outlaw hideout's mesa); the Baron's range continues off the map behind his fence line.

scenery.what: the La Plata Mountains, NW to W, about 20-30 km off, about 4,000 m (real)
the sunset notch: a low saddle in the western skyline due west of Main Street (bearing 270), kept clear of the rail line, which leaves 12 degrees north of it
the San Juan peaks and mesas, far north and north-east
Mesa country falling away south toward the San Juan River

speeds._doc: Travel times use these. The player's are the game's (config/movement/middle.tres). The horse isn't ridden yet (#341, #478): its gaits are PROPOSED from period horse numbers.

terrain._doc: How the generator makes the ground (the same function will bake Phase 2's height map): (1) a smooth surface through the control points [x, z, y] (thin-plate spline); (2) the creek, its canyon and the arroyo cut into it by their bed profiles and cross-sections (water.*); (3) level pads for the places (places.*.pad) and the town's plane (town.ground). Control points are the landform skeleton: the western foothills, the rail bench, the canyon rims, the lower north-east basin, the south-east upland, the southern mesas.

water._doc: Water flows downhill everywhere (the generator checks every bed profile falls). Clean Salt Creek rises in the south-west and passes the Southern Ute community and then the town's south edge before anything else touches it; the town's ditch takes water above town. The mine and Ore Works drain to the dry arroyo, which runs north of town and joins Salt Creek only at the north-east, below the widow's place (valley.md DECIDED: the mines' drainage bypasses town and joins downstream). Creek vertices: [x, z, bed_y, half_width, floor_half, wall_power]: the channel's rim half-width, its flat floor, the wall's curve (1 straight, 1.3 the trestle lab's gorge).

creek.status: DECIDED course (south of town, then to the trestle canyon); PROPOSED line and levels

canyon.name: Salt Creek Canyon (the great canyon)
canyon.status: DECIDED shape (deep and narrow at the trestle, carrying on south, widening and shallowing to a passable crossing); PROPOSED line
canyon._doc: The canyon is Salt Creek's own lower course, cut down through the rail bench where the creek drops toward the lower north-east basin. It runs about 520 m south (upstream) from the trestle to its head by Bridge A, shallowing from 27 m to about 3 m, and about 350 m north (downstream) of the trestle before it opens onto the widow's bottomland. Because water runs downhill, the shallow southern end is the UPSTREAM end: the brief's 'more passable farther downstream' is read as 'farther south'.

arroyo.flow: dry most of the year; flash floods after summer storms; steep cut banks 2-5 m; sand and cobble floor

heights_doc: #736 B (Sean, 2026-11-09): places with height, each a shooter above and a target below or the reverse, over the whole valley (and #736 A's landmark, rimrock and western water). PROPOSED, for Sean's changes before any is built. Each: `why`, who's `above` and `below`; `landform` (added to the ground by valley_plan.py's Terrain: `knoll`/`ridge`/`bluff`/`rim` a rounded rectangle `w` across `heading` by `d` along it, `h` m over the natural ground, falling to nothing over `run` m (`face`: the run on the side opposite the heading, the steep face; `profile` `cliff` straight, else a smoothstep), `butte` round (`w` across its top), `ledge` the ground raised to level `y` and `undercut` lowered to it (after the channels: a rock point over a canyon, a canyon's floor carried in under its rim), `notch` a gap in a rim (`x`, `w`, its walls' `run`); `at` its own middle when not the place's; `ramp` a wedge from a top edge to a foot); `blocks` (the greybox, ValleyMarkers: each `w` x `d` at `at` (the place's by default), `heading`, standing from the ground to `h` over its highest corner; `ladder` the one climbed, a Ladder on its side toward the crossroads; `stand` names a place on its top); `ladder_on` a place's own block to put the ladder on; `high` (the high spot: `at`, `over` m above the ground there: a roof, a platform); `targets` (from the high spot, measured by valley_plan.py: the distance and whether the line is clear); `place` when it gives height to a place already in `places`.

heights.name: Sentinel Butte (the landmark)
heights.why: The shape you steer by (#736 A1). 1.96 km due south of the crossroads, square down the North-South Street over the town bridge, so from town the way south is 'toward the butte'. 90 m over the southern mesas with a rock spire on its shoulder, above every skyline but the La Platas: seen from nine points in ten across the valley. Not west, so it never crowds the sunset notch.
heights.above: A lookout or a rifleman on the rim: the rimrock trail and the mesa overlook 200-350 m below; the whole south.
heights.below: Anyone on the rimrock trail or the hideout trail's top.

heights.name: The Baron's coach cut (the heist)
heights.why: On the coach's real route: the South Road is the Baron's own road between his headquarters and town (his town house, the bank, the depot), and this is its loneliest stretch, 0.9 km from the town bridge and 1.0 km from his headquarters, out of sight of both. The road climbs out of the creek bottoms at about 7 % into a cut through a low hogback: the team is slowest on the grade and the cut's 8 m banks won't let the coach swerve. The log deck sits on the south-west bank's lip, chained and wedged; its fall line meets the road at the top of the grade. The rimrock trail leaves the road 40 m on: the way out.
heights.above: The player at the log deck (18 m over the coach, revolver range) or on the outcrop opposite (40 m); the coach's outriders can take the outcrop too.
heights.below: The coach, its driver and guards in the cut; the road back toward town (200 m) and on toward the ranch (215 m) for whoever rides to help. The grade below the mouth is watched from the hogback's ends. The other ways: block the road in the cut, spook the team on the grade, take it at the bend below.

road_cut._doc: the South Road through the hogback 3 m over the natural ground: 8 m banks at 1:1.5, the grade up into it about 7 %

town._doc: The town to Sean's November 7 picture (DECIDED: its arrangement and spacing as drawn, Sean on #467 2026-11-07). Measured off the picture: Main Street's frontage, drawn 1,250 px long, is the DECIDED 250 m, so 5 px a metre along x; x = (picture px - 808) / 5 (808 is the North-South Street's middle). Across (z) the picture is a bird's-eye view, squeezed; its rows are kept in order and given period sizes (lots 125 ft deep, Main Street one surveyor's chain, 66 ft, wide; the rear alleys 20 ft). Lots are reservations ('x0', 'x1' along Main Street); what stands on them comes from the building lab's specs.

ground._doc: The town stands on a gentle slope: down 1.5 m along Main Street's 250 m to the east, and down from the rail bench (+2.8) to the creek bank (-4): about 4 % across, as a creek-side town on its terrace.

main_street.status: DECIDED 250 m; PROPOSED width (66 ft; the old street is 16.8 m)

walks._doc: PROPOSED (#737, waiting on Sean's changes): each building lot's `walk`: `h` its walk's top over the ground at its street edge's middle (m; each owner built his own, so the walks step up and down, the street's fall adding to it); `door` steps (default) or ramp; `w`/`e` its west/east end: steps (default: down to the ground, or to a lower neighbour's walk over a tight gap), ramp, or drop (no steps: jump); `awning` the eave over the walk (m; 0 none); `door_w` the door flight's width; `none` no walk; `why` the reason; `cellar` a lot's cellar: `rect` [x0, back0, x1, back1] (world x, metres back from the lot's front), its floor `below_floor` under the building's floor, `door` under_walk (doors under the walk at the street) or inside, `spec` where a building spec gives it. Rules: treads of at most `riser_max`, ramps 1 in `ramp_slope`; a walk `rail_at` or more over the dirt has a rail along its street edge (not at its flights or a drop) and from `posts_at` it stands on posts, open underneath.

back_street.status: DECIDED (deliveries and access behind the north side)

rear_lane.status: PROPOSED (behind the south side; the picture shows a lane there)

walk.why: A workshop: the floor kept low so planks and frames slide in off the lumber yard; two treads up. A hoist beam over the doors, no awning.
Stoves and nail kegs lifted off a wagon's tail by a man: knee height. Built first; the store went up beside it, higher.
The loading dock: level with a freight wagon's bed, so barrels and crates roll straight in. Its east end drops 1.1 m into the store alley: jump it, or go round by the steps.

cellar.why: The goods cellar: flour, salt pork and barrels kept cool, under the front half. Its doors open under the loading dock at the street: duck or crawl under the walk to reach them, or go down the stair behind the counter.

walk.why: Flour sacks carried in on a shoulder: just high enough to keep the street's dust out of the dough. A barrow ramp up to the butcher's.
Sides of beef carried straight off the wagon bed into the cold room.

walk.why: Wagon-bed height: barrels rolled off the brewer's dray onto the walk and in. The spec saloon's floor is 0.78 over its sill, so its lot stands 0.17 m up; its street balcony (3.66 m over the floor) is the walk's roof.

cellar.why: The spec saloon's cellar (Sean: yes, and big): kegs and spirits under the bar and the kitchen, the trap and its steep stair inside; the spec turned to face Main Street from the north puts it in the lot's east half, at the back. Its floor 2.4 m under the sill.

walk.why: Four easy steps for ladies in skirts and a man with a trunk: a long porch with chairs, a wide flight, the gallery over it.
The street falls away east; he kept his floor near the hotel's. A stretcher carried up five steps. (#765: the walk stops at his building; his side yard opens on Main Street by a wagon gate.)
